carousels.name: 4 facts about p*rn and erection problems most guys get wrong

slides.title: 4 facts about p*rn and erection problems [[most guys get wrong.]]
slides.sub: It's not just how much you watch.

slides.title: Had [[some]] ED
slides.body: In a study of 3,419 men aged 18–35 (JMIR Public Health and Surveillance), about 21% of those who'd tried sex in the past 4 weeks reported some degree of erectile dysfunction.

slides.title: Facts [[1–2]]
items: How often you watched wasn't linked to ED in that study.
Problematic use was — feeling out of control of your p*rn use.

slides.title: Facts [[3–4]]
items: One study can't prove cause — ED has many reasons, from stress to health.
Young doesn't mean immune. Erection problems happen in your 20s too.

slides.title: What to [[do]]
items: See a doctor — rule out physical causes first.
Be honest with them about your p*rn use.
Take a break from p*rn and notice what changes.
Ease the pressure — anxiety makes it worse.

carousels.name: 3 types of p*rn urges and how to beat each

slides.title: 3 types of p*rn urges [[— and how to beat each one.]]
slides.sub: Not every urge is the same. Don't fight them the same way.

slides.title: The [[bored]] urge
slides.body: Nothing to do, phone in hand, p*rn one tap away. Fix: give your hands a job — move, cook, build, call.

slides.title: The [[stressed]] urge
slides.body: A bad day wants an off switch, and p*rn feels like one. Fix: deal with the stress directly — walk, shower, write it down.

slides.title: The [[autopilot]] urge
slides.body: Same time, same place, same routine — your brain just runs the script. Fix: change the setting — the room, the time, what's in your hand.

slides.title: Name it [[first]]
items: Ask: bored, stressed or autopilot?
Pick the matching fix from this list.
Give it 10 minutes before deciding anything.
Note which type wins most this week.
slides.note: Which type hits you most? Comment 1, 2 or 3 👇

slides.title:

carousels.name: 5 rules for when you're home alone (NNN Day 21)

slides.title: 5 rules for when you're home alone [[and p*rn starts calling.]]
slides.sub: Day 21. An empty house is an invitation — don't accept it.

slides.title: Rules [[1–2]]
items: Leave the house first. Gym, café, walk — be out when the urge peaks.
No devices in the bedroom. Not "just for a minute."

slides.title: Rules [[3–4]]
items: Doors open, curtains open. Hiding is where p*rn lives.
Tell someone you're home alone today — let them check in.

slides.title: Don't [[test]] yourself
slides.body: "I'll be fine" is what everyone says right before they open p*rn. An empty house isn't a test. It's a trap. Plan around it.

slides.title: Before everyone [[leaves]]
items: Plan every block of empty hours.
Book something social for the evening.
Set a screen-time limit for the day.
Go to bed on time — late nights alone are the worst.

carousels.name: 5 signs p*rn is affecting your mental health

slides.title: 5 signs p*rn is affecting [[your mental health.]]
slides.sub: Not just your time. Your mood too.

slides.title: Signs [[1–3]]
items: You feel low or flat for hours after watching p*rn.
Your anxiety spikes when you try to stop.
You reach for p*rn every time a hard feeling shows up.

slides.title: Signs [[4–5]]
items: You've pulled away from people and things you used to enjoy.
Guilt and shame follow you into the next day.

slides.title: Research [[links]] them
slides.body: Studies have linked problematic p*rn use with more depression symptoms. They can't prove which comes first — but the two often feed each other.

slides.title: Look after [[yourself]]
items: Talk to a professional — a GP or counselor is a good start.
Tell one person how you've really been feeling.
Add one daily thing that lifts your mood — sunlight, movement, people.
If things feel dark, contact a crisis line or emergency services now.
